definition: rnn is an open-source machine learning framework that implements recurrent neural network architectures, such as LSTM and GRU, natively in the R programming language, that has been downloaded over 100,000 times (from the RStudio servers alone).
details: The rnn package is distributed through the Comprehensive R Archive Network under the open-source GPL v3 license.

explainer.lead: rnn is an open-source machine learning framework that implements recurrent neural network architectures such as LSTM and GRU natively in the R programming language. It has been downloaded over 100,000 times from the RStudio servers alone.

tiers.eli5: Like a toolkit built specifically for R users so they don't have to switch languages to build sequence models.
tiers.practitioner: R users reach for it to build LSTM and GRU models without leaving the R ecosystem. A pitfall is that it is an R-native implementation rather than a bridge to a larger framework.
tiers.paperLevel: A framework implementing recurrent neural network architectures natively in R; distributed through CRAN under the open-source GPL v3 license.

explainer.example: An R analyst fits an LSTM to a time series using the package's native R implementation of the architecture.
